title: Craftsman  -  One Log, Four Useful Planks
design_overview:
Craftsman  -  One Log, Four Useful Planks

**Premise and dialogue:** Turn a precise material into a useful building supply while learning that a craftsman needs an output instruction. “A workshop needs more than a table. Tell me what you want made, show me the materials, and I'll make your first batch free.”

**Existing:** CRAFTSMAN requires a work area, crafting table and target filter/recipe. It gathers exact inputs, crafts with remainders and deposits output. Prefer First, Round Robin and Forced Round Robin modes already exist. This first lesson uses a single target; it does not require settlement-managed queues or recursive crafting.

**Target:** one validated oak-log-to-oak-planks crafting operation, normally four planks. Runtime validation determines exact ingredient/result count; if unavailable, pick another explicit simple supported crafting recipe rather than manufacture it.

steps.title: 1 Accept the first commission
steps.design_check: player/job record reserved, worker bound and no conflicting managed order.
steps.design_provisions: one-operation free assignment and shared Clipboard if needed.
steps.design_notes:
1 Accept the first commission

**Tutor:** “Give me one small commission, and I'll show you how I work.”

**Check:** player/job record reserved, worker bound and no conflicting managed order.

**Provides:** one-operation free assignment and shared Clipboard if needed.

steps.title: 2 Mark the workshop

cards.text: Open {Inventory}. Right-click the Clipboard slot until it reads Edit Job Site, then close the inventory. With it in your hand, point at our crafting table and press {Use}.

See the box? Scroll to move it, or hold {ControlModifier} while scrolling to make it wider or narrower. Hold {ShiftModifier} and scroll to change its height position; {ControlModifier} and {AltModifier} together change its height. Include the work and a clear way to reach it.
When the box fits, point at me, your Craftsman, and press {Use} without sneaking. Show me the area you chose.

sequences.confirmation_guidance: Preview our crafting table, then acknowledge the actual saved area on the bound Craftsman. Do not complete for moving or merely displaying the box.
sequences.recovery: That is only the draft until you apply it to me. If it is in the wrong place, point at the right centre and use the Clipboard again. To start fresh, hold {Sneak} and press {Attack} on a block in Edit Job Site, then redraw. Keep protected or unrelated work outside.

steps.design_objective: Apply a work area containing a reachable crafting table.
steps.design_check: persisted assignment and the worker's actual table/path validation.
steps.design_provisions: provenance-tracked table loan or existing fixture, plus missing-table versus unreachable-table guidance.
steps.design_notes:
2 Mark the workshop

**Teach and demonstrate (spoken in order):**
1. “Open {Inventory}. Right-click the Clipboard slot until it reads Edit Job Site, then close the inventory. With it in your hand, point at our crafting table and press {Use}.”
2. “See the box? Scroll to move it, or hold Control while scrolling to make it wider or narrower. Hold Shift and scroll to change its height position; Control and Alt together change its height. Include the work and a clear way to reach it.”
3. “When the box fits, point at me, your Craftsman, and press {Use} without sneaking. Show me the area you chose.”

**Show / confirm:** Preview our crafting table, then acknowledge the actual saved area on the bound Craftsman. Do not complete for moving or merely displaying the box.

**If it goes wrong:** “That is only the draft until you apply it to me. If it is in the wrong place, point at the right centre and use the Clipboard again. To start fresh, hold {Sneak} and press {Attack} on a block in Edit Job Site, then redraw. Keep protected or unrelated work outside.”


**Optional flavour line:** “Mark the table where you want me to craft. Leave me room to reach it.”

**Task:** Apply a work area containing a reachable crafting table.

**Check:** persisted assignment and the worker's actual table/path validation.

**Provides:** provenance-tracked table loan or existing fixture, plus missing-table versus unreachable-table guidance.

steps.title: 3 Connect material and finished-stock chests

cards.text: Open {Inventory} and right-click the Clipboard slot until a storage mode appears. Close the inventory and hold your Clipboard. Hold {ControlModifier} and scroll until it says Assign Supplies.
Point at the supplies chest and press {Use}. That selects the chest; it has not assigned it yet.
Now point at me, your Craftsman, and press {Use} without sneaking. Click Assign Clipboard Storage in the menu. Show me that last step.

sequences.confirmation_guidance: Identify this lesson’s supplies chest and named tutor. Show selection first, then acknowledge only the stored Supplies link for this worker. Opening the menu is an intermediate checkpoint.
sequences.recovery: If you selected the wrong chest, close the menu, aim into empty air, hold {Sneak} and press {Use} with the Clipboard to clear the selection. Select the right chest and choose Assign Clipboard Storage again. If you cannot open the chest to load it, put the Clipboard away first.

cards.text: Open {Inventory} and right-click the Clipboard slot until a storage mode appears. Close the inventory and hold your Clipboard. Hold {ControlModifier} and scroll until it says Assign Output Storage.
Point at the output chest and press {Use}. That selects the chest; it has not assigned it yet.
Now point at me, your Craftsman, and press {Use} without sneaking. Click Assign Clipboard Storage in the menu. Show me that last step.

sequences.confirmation_guidance: Identify this lesson’s output chest and named tutor. Show selection first, then acknowledge only the stored Output link for this worker. Opening the menu is an intermediate checkpoint.
sequences.recovery: If you selected the wrong chest, close the menu, aim into empty air, hold {Sneak} and press {Use} with the Clipboard to clear the selection. Select the right chest and choose Assign Clipboard Storage again. If you cannot open the chest to load it, put the Clipboard away first.

steps.design_objective: Assign Supplies and Output using the clipboard.
steps.design_check: reachable assigned containers, filters and result/remainder capacity.
steps.design_provisions: container loans if necessary and a clear material-flow preview.

steps.title: 4 Specify the output

cards.text: Hold the lesson Recipe Filter in your main hand. Aim into empty air and press {Use} without sneaking. Click the < or > arrows until the oak-log-to-oak-planks recipe is shown. Check the ingredient and four-plank result.

Click the recipe filter mode button until it reads Deny (Deny Matching). This deliberately excludes the selected recipe output. Close the editor; do not hold {Sneak} while using the filter, because that clears it.

Keep the configured Recipe Filter in your main hand, point at me, your bound Craftsman, and press {Use}. Choose Assign configured filter. That installs the filter with its saved mode. Opening this menu alone does not assign it. Keep any returned previous filter safely.
Return to this lesson and choose Check my committed result. Work stays within the same finite trial; do not start work while this deliberately wrong mode is installed.

sequences.confirmation_guidance: Verify a real successful filter assignment by this player to the bound Craftsman and the installed recipe/mode. An edited held filter or opened menu is insufficient.
sequences.recovery: Use the arrows to select the actual one-log, four-plank recipe. Set Deny Matching, then hold the filter, press {Use} on the bound Craftsman and choose Assign configured filter. If that recipe is unavailable, stop and report the missing runtime recipe.

cards.text: Put the filter and Clipboard away. With an empty hand, press {Use} on me and reopen this Craftsman lesson. Choose Show me exactly how, then Check my committed result on this card. I will evaluate the filter installed on this worker against oak planks.

Deny Matching excludes our selected oak-plank output; other outputs can still match. Choose Check my committed result to receive the server-confirmed result before changing anything. This is a filter check, not a completed craft.

sequences.confirmation_guidance: Check the installed filter on the server; no menu-open, task-start or old item grants productive credit.
sequences.recovery: Keep the installed oak-planks Recipe Filter in Deny Matching. Ask me to check it before correcting it; changing only a held copy cannot change the worker.

cards.text: With the Clipboard put away, press {Use} on me with an empty hand. Choose Job > Job Inventory. Left-click the installed Recipe Filter in my filter slot, then an empty player inventory slot to retrieve it. Close the menu and put it in your main hand.

Aim into empty air and press {Use} without sneaking. Keep the same oak-planks recipe and click the mode button until Allow (Allow Matching) appears. Close the editor, hold that filter, press {Use} on me and choose Assign configured filter again.

Return to this lesson and choose Check my committed result. I check the correction was assigned after the exclusion was observed, and that oak planks now match. Then put the Clipboard away, press {Use} on the supplies chest with an empty hand, and place the allocated oak log inside. The later work step still requires one real craft and delivery.

sequences.confirmation_guidance: Check the installed filter on the server; no menu-open, task-start or old item grants productive credit.
sequences.recovery: Retrieve the installed filter through Job > Job Inventory. Correct its mode to Allow Matching and use it on the same Craftsman, then choose Assign configured filter. Supplies, reachable table and output room are still required.

cards.text: Put the Clipboard away. With an empty hand, press {Use} on me, then choose Job and Work Settings.
Click the craftsman mode control until Prefer First is reported. For this lesson keep only our one explicit target recipe.
Show me those settings. We will begin once they are right.

sequences.confirmation_guidance: Read back the server-confirmed settings on this tutor; highlight only the next requested option.
sequences.recovery: If you opened the Clipboard storage menu, close it and put the Clipboard away before talking to me again. If Job is unavailable, the lesson must restore your trial assignment; do not buy a paid hire to get past the tutorial.

steps.design_objective: Configure and assign an excluding Recipe Filter, observe the committed matching result, then correct and reassign it before the finite one-craft trial.
steps.design_check: server resolves a supported crafting target and exact input alternatives.
steps.design_provisions: a configured filter loan or guided filter configuration and one matching log once. Explain one recipe operation may produce several items.
steps.design_notes:
4 Specify the output

The personal filter follow-up extends the original v1 setup with committed configure, assign, observe and adjust checkpoints.

With the Clipboard put away, press {Use} on me with an empty hand. Choose Job > Job Inventory. Left-click the installed Recipe Filter in my filter slot, then an empty player inventory slot to retrieve it. Close the menu and put it in your main hand.

Sequence step_4_sequence_2
Put the Clipboard away. With an empty hand, press {Use} on me, then choose Job and Work Settings.

steps.title: 5 Let the worker craft

cards.text: Put the Clipboard away. With an empty hand, press {Use} on me, then choose Job and Work Settings.
Choose Ask for Work Report first. If work is paused, click Start/Pause Work once. Leave it alone if work is already enabled, then close the conversation so I can work.
Show me those settings. We will begin once they are right.

sequences.confirmation_guidance: Confirm work-enabled authority for this finite trial and show the real next worker action. Starting work is not evidence that the harvest, craft or delivery succeeded.
sequences.recovery: If you opened the Clipboard storage menu, close it and put the Clipboard away before talking to me again. If Job is unavailable, the lesson must restore your trial assignment; do not buy a paid hire to get past the tutorial.

steps.design_check: the worker gathers the allocated log, reaches the table and successfully applies the carried recipe, consuming the real input and retaining any recipe remainders.
steps.design_provisions: “moving,” “missing material,” “crafting” or “output full” feedback. New tutorial authority caps recipe operations and exact permitted inputs so nearby stock is not consumed freely.
steps.design_notes:
5 Let the worker craft

**Teach and demonstrate (spoken in order):**
1. “Put the Clipboard away. With an empty hand, press {Use} on me, then choose Job and Work Settings.”
2. “Choose Ask for Work Report first. If work is paused, click Start/Pause Work once. Leave it alone if work is already enabled, then close the conversation so I can work.”
3. “Show me those settings. We will begin once they are right.”

**Show / confirm:** Confirm work-enabled authority for this finite trial and show the real next worker action. Starting work is not evidence that the harvest, craft or delivery succeeded.

**If it goes wrong:** “If you opened the Clipboard storage menu, close it and put the Clipboard away before talking to me again. If Job is unavailable, the lesson must restore your trial assignment; do not buy a paid hire to get past the tutorial.”


**Optional flavour line:** “Now I can bring the log to the table and turn it into something useful.”

**Task:** Enable work.

**Check:** the worker gathers the allocated log, reaches the table and successfully applies the carried recipe, consuming the real input and retaining any recipe remainders.

**Provides:** “moving,” “missing material,” “crafting” or “output full” feedback. New tutorial authority caps recipe operations and exact permitted inputs so nearby stock is not consumed freely.

steps.title: 6 Receive the batch

cards.text: Put the Clipboard away. With an empty hand, press {Use} on the output chest to open it and look at what arrived.
Close the chest, then press {Use} on me, your Craftsman, with an empty hand. Return to our lesson conversation.

sequences.confirmation_guidance: Show the attributable delivered goods and actual remaining amount. Reopening a chest or saying “done” never substitutes for the delivery receipt.
sequences.recovery: If it is empty, leave room in the output chest and ask me for a Work Report under Job → Work Settings. Follow the missing supplies, blocked path or full-output hint; moving your own matching items into it will not complete my work.

steps.design_objective: Inspect Output and return to the craftsman.
steps.design_check: the actual recipe result count from this allocation is deposited, not pre-existing player-made planks.
steps.design_notes:
6 Receive the batch

**Teach and demonstrate (spoken in order):**
1. “Put the Clipboard away. With an empty hand, press {Use} on the output chest to open it and look at what arrived.”
2. “Close the chest, then press {Use} on me, your Craftsman, with an empty hand. Return to our lesson conversation.”

**Show / confirm:** Show the attributable delivered goods and actual remaining amount. Reopening a chest or saying “done” never substitutes for the delivery receipt.

**If it goes wrong:** “If it is empty, leave room in the output chest and ask me for a Work Report under Job → Work Settings. Follow the missing supplies, blocked path or full-output hint; moving your own matching items into it will not complete my work.”


**Optional flavour line:** “There are your planks. Would you like to discuss the next commission?”

**Task:** Inspect Output and return to the craftsman.

**Check:** the actual recipe result count from this allocation is deposited, not pre-existing player-made planks.

**Provides/reward:** those planks and reusable configuration. “One log turned into supplies you can use. Want the next batch? Here's my normal rate.” Apply shared ending.

**A Continue working:** “Show me your normal price.” Present the current role, duration, currency and total. Start ordinary paid work only after the player accepts a still-valid quote.

**B Stop here:** “Thanks. Stop working.” End this tutorial assignment safely, reconcile its output and identifiable loans, and keep the lesson completed. Dismissal leaves work paused.


**New hooks:** filter/recipe resolution; committed work area/table readiness; successful HiredSupplyCrafting.applyCarriedRecipe attribution; result and remainder bookkeeping; output deposit. Count both recipe operations and result quantities to avoid treating four-output recipes as four free operations. Crafting success alone is not delivery.
